decks.domain: License requirements, identification and learner licenses

cards.front: Which Alabama residents need a driver license, and what is the one exception?
cards.back: Every Alabama resident who drives a motor vehicle needs a driver license, except when temporarily moving a farm tractor or implement of husbandry on a road.

cards.front: Who must pass the driver exam, and when does an expired out-of-state license need none?
cards.back: Anyone never licensed in Alabama, or whose Alabama license expired more than three years ago, must pass the driver exam; an out-of-state license expired one year or less needs no exam.

cards.front: How does the expiry cutoff that triggers an exam differ for Alabama and out-of-state licenses?
cards.back: An expired Alabama license triggers a new exam after more than three years, but an expired out-of-state license triggers one after more than one year.

cards.front: When may a federal employee drive in Alabama without an Alabama license?
cards.back: A federal employee driving a vehicle owned or leased by the U.S. government needs no Alabama license for that driving.

cards.front: Which residents may drive without an Alabama license because of a license from elsewhere?
cards.back: A resident aged sixteen or older carrying a valid home-state or home-country license may drive without an Alabama one, including out-of-state military families stationed here on long assignments.

cards.front: How long may a visitor from a country that does not license drivers drive here, and on what condition?
cards.back: A non-resident aged sixteen or older from a country that does not license drivers may drive here up to ninety days per calendar year if the vehicle is registered for the current year at home.

cards.front: How long may a new resident drive on the previous state's license?
cards.back: A new resident with a valid license from the previous state may drive on it for thirty days after moving to Alabama.

cards.front: How does the new resident window differ from the yearly limit for visitors from non-licensing countries?
cards.back: A new resident may drive on the old state's license for thirty days, which is a different window from the ninety-day yearly limit for visitors from countries that do not license drivers.

cards.front: Which non-resident students may drive here on a valid home license?
cards.back: A non-resident full-time student enrolled at an Alabama school, college or trade school may drive on a valid home license.

decks.domain: License requirements, identification and learner licenses

cards.front: Which three kinds of applicants will Alabama refuse to license?
cards.back: Alabama will not license anyone under sixteen, anyone suspended or revoked in any state, or anyone who fails a required exam.

cards.front: What health or substance problems lead Alabama to refuse a license?
cards.back: A license is also refused to a habitual drunkard or narcotics addict, or to someone whose physical or mental impairment, in the view of ALEA or the examiner, would prevent ordinary control of a vehicle.

cards.front: What school requirement applies to applicants under nineteen?
cards.back: Applicants under nineteen must meet Alabama Act ninety-three-three hundred sixty-eight, which calls for secondary school graduation or current attendance, with limited exclusions.

cards.front: How does the minimum licensing age differ from the under-nineteen school rule?
cards.back: The minimum licensing age is sixteen, but the separate under-nineteen rule ties licensing to school graduation or attendance under Act ninety-three-three hundred sixty-eight.
cards.memory_hook: sixteen to drive, school till nineteen

cards.front: What must every applicant for an original license or ID card prove?
cards.back: Every applicant for an original Alabama license or ID card must prove authorized presence in the United States under federal law.

decks.domain: License requirements, identification and learner licenses

cards.front: What document combinations prove identification, and what must every combination include?
cards.back: For identification you bring two documents with at least one bearing a photo, or three non-photo documents, and either way one must be from the Primary Listing.

cards.front: How do the two-document and three-document identification paths differ on photos?
cards.back: The two-document identification path needs at least one photo document, while the three-document path may be all non-photo, and both need one Primary Listing item.

cards.front: What must you show to transfer an out-of-state license?
cards.back: To transfer an out-of-state license you show that license, a Social Security card or other accepted number proof, and one more Primary Listing document.

cards.front: What can prove your birth date, and what is accepted when no prior Alabama record exists?
cards.back: A prior Alabama license or ID record can prove your birth date; without one, only an original or certified Primary Listing document is accepted.

cards.front: What kinds of documents are accepted, and what must a certified copy carry?
cards.back: Only originals or agency-certified copies are accepted, and a certified copy must carry an original certification.

cards.front: What problems with a document cause it to be rejected?
cards.back: A document is rejected when key details show white-out, erasures or alterations, are missing or unreadable, are hidden by a fold, tear, hole or staple, or when it is not properly signed.

cards.front: What must a notarized document show to be accepted?
cards.back: A notarized document needs a readable seal or stamp, the notary's readable name, a signature, the state of commission, and a commission expiration date still current when notarized.

cards.front: Which documents appear on the Primary Listing?
cards.back: Primary documents include a certified U.S. birth certificate, an unexpired U.S. passport, an Alabama license or ID, a naturalization or citizenship certificate, and a valid foreign passport with a U.S. immigration document.

cards.front: What birth certificate must every fifteen-year-old applicant show, and what applies to a foreign one?
cards.back: Every fifteen-year-old applicant must show a certified U.S. birth certificate, and a foreign birth certificate must be translated into English and embassy-certified unless the person has a U.S. passport.

cards.front: Which documents appear on the secondary list?
cards.back: Secondary documents include a marriage license, a military ID or DD-two hundred fourteen, a school photo ID, a certified school record, and court decrees such as divorce, adoption or name change.

decks.module: Number proof, immigration and test languages
decks.domain: License requirements, identification and learner licenses

cards.front: When must you prove your Social Security number?
cards.back: Social Security number proof is needed for any license class, renewal, vessel license or ID card unless the number is on file, even if you do not want it printed.
cards.memory_hook: no number on file, prove it

cards.front: What counts as Social Security number proof, and what must it show?
cards.back: That proof must be an original showing all nine digits, such as the card, a certified Social Security Administration letter, form DD two hundred fourteen, a W2, or a Medicare or Medicaid card whose number ends in A.

cards.front: How much permitted stay must immigration documents show?
cards.back: Immigration documents must show at least thirty days of permitted stay remaining in the United States.

cards.front: What extra documents may non-citizens add to their application?
cards.back: Non-citizens may add documents such as an Employment Authorization Document with a valid Social Security card, a visa allowing more than thirty days of stay, or a valid I-ninety-four record.

cards.front: Which languages does the list of written exams include?
cards.back: Written exams are offered in Arabic, Chinese, Farsi, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, Thai and Vietnamese.

cards.front: What option exists for an applicant who cannot read and understand the knowledge test?
cards.back: An applicant unable to read and understand the knowledge test may take an oral exam, which the automated testing equipment can deliver.

decks.domain: License requirements, identification and learner licenses

cards.front: When did Alabama's graduated license law take effect, and what minimum driving age does it set?
cards.back: Alabama's graduated license law took effect October one, two thousand two, and the minimum driving age is sixteen, with certain exceptions and restrictions.

cards.front: What can you earn at fifteen, and what license class and restriction does it give?
cards.back: At fifteen you can earn a restricted Learner License by passing an exam drawn from this manual, giving a Class D license with a Y restriction.

cards.front: Who may sit beside a Y-restricted learner who is not yet sixteen?
cards.back: Before age sixteen a Y-restricted learner drives only with a licensed Alabama driver aged twenty-one or older, or a licensed or certified instructor, in the seat beside them.

cards.front: Who may sit beside a learner after the sixteenth birthday, and how long does the license issued at fifteen last?
cards.back: After the sixteenth birthday any licensed driver may sit beside the learner, and the license issued at fifteen lasts four years and can be renewed once.

cards.front: How does the companion rule for a fifteen-year-old learner change after the sixteenth birthday?
cards.back: A learner aged fifteen needs a companion who is a licensed Alabama driver aged twenty-one or older or a driving instructor, while after the sixteenth birthday any licensed driver may ride beside them.

cards.front: How long does the learner license issued at fifteen stay valid, and how often may it be renewed?
cards.back: The learner license issued at fifteen stays valid for four years and may be renewed only one time.

cards.front: What restriction and term apply to a learner license earned at sixteen or older?
cards.back: A Learner License earned at sixteen or older also carries the Y restriction, requiring a licensed driver beside you, and is valid for four years.

cards.front: What companion does a learner licensed at sixteen or older need?
cards.back: A learner license earned at sixteen or older needs only a licensed driver beside you, unlike the stricter companion rule that applies before age sixteen.

cards.front: For what reasons can a learner license be suspended or revoked?
cards.back: A Learner License can be suspended or revoked for the same causes as a driver license, and also revoked for breaking its own terms.

decks.domain: License requirements, identification and learner licenses

cards.front: When may a driver from sixteen to under eighteen take the road test?
cards.back: A driver from sixteen to under eighteen may take the road test after holding a learner license, including a comparable out-of-state one, for six months or until turning eighteen.

cards.front: What holding period must drivers sixteen to under eighteen complete before the road test?
cards.back: Drivers aged sixteen to under eighteen must hold the learner license for six months or until turning eighteen before taking the road test.

cards.front: What happens to the learner license and the Y restriction at the road test?
cards.back: You surrender the learner license at the road test, and passing removes the Y restriction for the rest of the four-year period at no cost.

cards.front: Does removing the Y restriction after the road test start a new license term?
cards.back: Removing the Y restriction after the road test does not start a new term: the regular license runs only for the remainder of the original four-year period.

cards.front: What license can a fourteen or fifteen-year-old get for a small motor driven cycle?
cards.back: At fourteen or fifteen you can get a Class M license with a B restriction for a motor driven cycle of at most two hundred pounds and one hundred fifty cubic centimeters engine displacement.

cards.front: What does a Class M license cover from age sixteen?
cards.back: From sixteen a Class M license covers motorcycles only, meaning vehicles with a rider's seat or saddle built to run on no more than three wheels on the ground, tractors excluded.

cards.front: How does the Class D learner license differ from the B-restricted Class M license?
cards.back: Class D with a Y restriction is the car learner license, whereas Class M with a B restriction is limited to motor driven cycles for riders aged fourteen or fifteen.
cards.memory_hook: D for cars, M for cycles

cards.front: What restrictions may the ALEA Director add, and what can violating one cost?
cards.back: The ALEA Director may add restrictions needed for safe driving, such as corrective lenses or mechanical aids, and violating one can cost you the license.

cards.front: From what age is a vessel license available, and how is it earned?
cards.back: A vessel license is available from age twelve by passing the vessel exam at a license office or showing an approved boating safety course certificate.

recap_hooks.text: Every Alabama resident who drives needs a license, and an exam is required after an Alabama license lapses over three years or an out-of-state one over one year.

Some drivers may skip an Alabama license for a while: new residents for thirty days, visitors from non-licensing countries up to ninety days a year, plus federal employees, licensed residents and non-resident students.
Alabama refuses anyone under sixteen, anyone suspended or revoked, anyone failing an exam, and anyone whose addiction or impairment prevents ordinary vehicle control.
Applicants under nineteen must also meet the school graduation or attendance rule, and every original applicant proves authorized presence.
Identification takes two documents with a photo or three without, always including one Primary Listing item, and only originals or certified copies count.
Altered, unreadable or unsigned papers are rejected, notarized papers need a readable seal and current commission, and every fifteen-year-old shows a certified birth certificate.

recaps.module: Number proof, immigration and test languages

recap_hooks.text: Social Security number proof is needed unless the number is on file, and it must be an original showing all nine digits.
Immigration papers need at least thirty days of stay left, written exams come in eleven listed languages, and an oral exam serves those who cannot read the test.
A learner license earned at fifteen is Class D with a Y restriction, and before sixteen the companion must be a licensed Alabama driver at least twenty-one or an instructor.
From sixteen any licensed driver may ride beside the learner; the license issued at fifteen lasts four years and renews once, and a learner license can be suspended or revoked.
Drivers sixteen to under eighteen hold the learner license six months or until eighteen before the road test, and passing drops the Y restriction for the rest of the same term.
Class M with a B restriction covers small motor driven cycles at fourteen or fifteen, full Class M covers motorcycles from sixteen, and vessel licenses start at twelve.
